name: Noah
testimonial: Fictional internal review draft: My dog usually bolts when the clippers come out, but he scratched this for treats on day one. way less drama.

name: Lucas
testimonial: I wanted something for between groomer visits, not another wrestling match. This board made the routine feel simple n easy.

name: Charlotte
testimonial: Not instant, but after a few short sessions I could hear less clicking on the floor. that alone felt worth it.

name: Oliver
testimonial: The best part was not having to hold her paw still. She chose to come back for another scratch because of the treats.

name: Theodore
testimonial: My staffy did not fully get it right away, but with treats and two calm tries she started using it. honest 8 from me.

name: Olivia
testimonial: We bought the 2-board set so one stays downstairs and one upstairs. For a busy house, thats actually super handy.

name: Luca
testimonial: I was mainly after a lower-stress option for my rescue dog. Clippers made him stiff and weird, this felt much calmer because he could choose to engage instead of being pinned in place. I still supervise it and I know it is really for front nails, but for that job it fits our routine better than the old panic session ever did.

name: Evie
testimonial: It definitely isn't a magic fix, but it gave me a routine I can actually stick to. A couple of short sessions through the week feels more doable than building up dread for one big nail clip day.

name: Charlie
testimonial: My kelpie mix is smart but dramatic about paw handling. Once she realised scratching the board made treats appear, she was way more interested than I expected. I like that I can keep front nails in check without feeling like the bad guy every single time.

name: Ava
testimonial: What sold me was the lower-pressure setup. I sit on the floor, load a few treats, and let my dog work it out. It feels less like a fight and more like a little training game, which is a huge emotional difference in our house.

name: Archie
testimonial: I bought it because the clicking on our floors was getting full on annoying. After repeated use the front nails sounded less sharp, and the greetings stopped feeling so scratchy on bare legs. Not a miracle overnight thing, just a practical improvement.

name: Oscar
testimonial: Delivery took a bit, but once it arrived the concept was easy to understand. My dog needed a few tries, so I'm rating it an 8 not a 10, but I still prefer this over wrestling with clippers.

name: Grace
testimonial: For me the value is that I can do upkeep at home instead of waiting until things get too long and stressful. It fills that in-between gap really well.

name: Hugo
testimonial: My puppy took to it faster than expected because it just felt like a reward game. I like starting the paw-care habit this way instead of waiting until she's older and already hates nail trims.

name: Matilda
testimonial: I was worried my bigger dog would ignore it, but he actually leaned into the scratch motion once food was involved. We still keep sessions short, and I treat it as front-nail maintenance rather than the whole answer, but it has been a solid tool to have around.

name: Amelia
testimonial: The emotional win was huge tbh. No hiding dog, no me putting it off for days, no guilty feeling after. Just a quick supervised routine and done.

name: Sienna
testimonial: Our dog did not instantly understand the board, so I can't call it effortless. But once we paired it with good treats and repeated short sessions, it became way easier than clipping. That feels fair to say.

name: Layla
testimonial: I like that it gives me something repeatable. Same board, same treats, same quick routine. In a house with two dogs and not much spare time, repeatable is kind of everything.

name: Henry
testimonial: I bought this after another failed clipper attempt where my dog pulled away so hard I just gave up. What I wanted was not perfection, just a calmer way to stay on top of front nails at home. The board felt easier on both of us because I was not trying to pin a paw still and he was working for treats instead of bracing for a cut. I noticed the biggest difference when I kept sessions short and regular rather than expecting one big result. It also helped with the scratchy jumping-up moments on my legs. For our house, that lower-conflict routine is the real product.

name: Sophie
testimonial: We use it as upkeep between groomer appointments, and that framing helped me. I am not expecting salon-level results in one go. I am expecting less floor clicking, fewer sharp greetings, and less stress in our week, and it has delivered on that so far.

name: Zara
testimonial: The no-drama part is what mattered most to me. My dog had gotten weirdly tense around any paw touching, and I hated being the person causing that. With this, the energy shifted. He approached it like a game, and I could finally participate in nail upkeep without that awful pit in my stomach. I still watch him the whole time, and I know the board is mainly for front nails, but that honesty actually made me trust it more.

name: Georgia
testimonial: As someone with a newly adopted dog, I wanted a habit we could build without starting our relationship with forced nail clipping. The board gave us a more cooperative routine. He did not master it instantly, but he understood the reward pretty quickly, and that was enough to keep going. I appreciate that I can use it in short bursts instead of setting aside a big stressful session.

name: Finn
testimonial: I almost skipped it because I wasn't sure my dog would scratch on cue. Fair question honestly. In our case she needed a little encouragement and decent treats, then it clicked. What I like now is how little owner skill it takes compared with clipping. I don't need perfect timing with clippers or a second person to hold her. I just supervise, keep the session short, and let her do the scratching work.

name: Jack
testimonial: My partner and I ended up getting the 2-board option because we kept moving one board around the house in our heads before even buying. That turned out to be the right call. One stays where the dog usually settles and the other is near the back door, so we actually remember to use them. The product only makes sense if it becomes part of normal life, and for us the extra board removed friction.

name: William
testimonial: My dog is the type to hear the clipper case open and disappear. That alone should tell you how nail day used to go. The board changed the starting point because I was no longer trying to grab a paw and rush through it before he panicked. Instead I could sit with him, hide a few treats, and reward the scratch motion. The result has been gradual, not dramatic, but the whole household feels less tense around grooming now.

name: Archer
testimonial: We have polished floors, so long front nails are impossible to ignore in this house. The sound was driving me mad and guests were noticing the scratchy greetings too. I wanted a maintenance tool, not another chore that required courage. This worked best when I treated it like a tiny daily game. Once I stopped expecting an instant fix, I started appreciating how easy it was to repeat.

name: Hamish
testimonial: I am not very coordinated with clippers and always felt like one wrong move would make the experience worse for both of us. This product felt more beginner-friendly because the process is basically set the board down, add treats, supervise, repeat. My dog still had to learn it, but once he understood the game I felt much more confident handling upkeep at home.

name: Hudson
testimonial: We bought the household pack because there are multiple dogs here and tools vanish between rooms in this house lol. What I like is that the routine feels consistent no matter which dog is up next. Treats in, board down, supervise, a few scratches, done. It is not some giant transformation in one afternoon, but it has cut down the chaos around front-nail upkeep and that is a win in a multi-dog home.

name: Muhammad
testimonial: I needed something that matched my dog's behaviour instead of fighting it. She already likes pawing at things when she's excited, so giving that scratching impulse a better outlet made sense. The board turned that natural movement into a useful little habit for front nails. I still keep expectations realistic, but the fact that she participates willingly makes all the difference.

name: Mila
testimonial: The thing I would tell a friend is this: buy it if you want a calmer front-nail maintenance routine, not if you want an instant one-and-done replacement for every grooming task. In that lane, it has been really good for us. My dog stopped treating nail care like a betrayal, and I stopped postponing it until the clicking got ridiculous. That change in consistency has probably been the biggest benefit.

name: Ella
testimonial: This ended up being one of those products that lowers the temperature in the house. Before, nail care meant me procrastinating, my dog reading my stress, and the whole thing snowballing. Now I can pull out the board, add treats, and do a quick supervised session before either of us has time to get worked up. The gradual front-nail filing suits us better than direct clipping ever did. It feels sustainable, and thats why I'd keep using it.
